doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The orchestra's goal accomplished and Irakere's origin
summary: Its splendor lasted one or two years; once it removed the anti-jazz accusation against the government, it faded, and Irakere followed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: How many years did that orchestra last?

Many years, but the splendor of the orchestra last maybe one year, two at the most, because the orchestra accomplish its goal. That was taking away from the government the accusations of anti-Jazz, anti-foreigner accusations. That’s all they want; they want to erase the image that, ‘Jazz isn’t our type of music and we don’t want nothing that is coming from outside.’ As soon as they accomplished that—
So, the orchestra served the government well?
Yea, and we were happy to do it. See, we play the music; we wanted to do it to play music. So, they let us play the music and then after two years—that’s why Irakere was born also then.
